profiles.nativeOtClientV8Detail: experimental 740 login, character selection, map, movement, shared-player visibility, bounded player-vitals updates, typed no-output map/creature look request handling, and a parser-shaped empty Quest Log acknowledgement. The player-stats record has parser-shaped 16-bit level and soul fields, but unmodified-client confirmation remains required
profiles.localCharacterProvisioningDetail: local SQLite/Argon2 account provisioning and additive character creation persist the exact classic cumulative experience threshold for the returned level-eight default, so later authoritative experience awards cannot reduce a newly created character's level. The stable player create command preserves its original account/name form and accepts an optional validated u16 vocation ID that is durable at insertion; no label-to-vocation inference is claimed. Existing externally created or legacy inconsistent character records are not rewritten automatically
profiles.legacyItemMetadataDetail: bounded operator-supplied items.xml armor, defense, extra-defense, attack-speed, and verified weapon-type labels are retained only for known OTB items. The parsed fields do not alter FE combat, equipment behavior, packets, or compatibility claims. Formula use remains deferred until profile-specific slot, vocation, fight-mode, active-block, and controlled-randomness evidence is implemented
profiles.runtimeItemsAndInventoryDetail: bounded item/equipment/container core, SQLite equipment/container persistence, native-session hydration, catalog-validated classic-740 initial equipment delivery, and stable operator commands that atomically move a complete item from equipment into one owned bounded top-level container or from an owned container item index into an empty equipment slot. Occupied slots, missing containers, and invalid indices leave authoritative state unchanged. A shared authoritative equipment replacement advances a dedicated epoch; a native session compares only catalog-mapped slots already sent at login and emits deterministic parser-verified SetInventory or DeleteInventory records for a changed, removed, or newly unmapped slot. A real shared container replacement advances a dedicated epoch and re-emits only current complete catalog-mapped top-level open-container records. Native 740 CloseContainer (0x87) is decoded as one client-view container ID and receives the parser-verified 0x6F close record; that session ID is excluded from later container refreshes without mutating shared or persisted data. Native 740 UpdateContainer (0xCA) requests one complete mapped top-level container for the current session, sends its existing parser-verified 0x6E record when available, and removes that ID from the closed-view set without mutating shared or persisted data. The existing complete-item equipment/container transactions are also available under the shared world lock and advance both refresh epochs only after core success; rejected moves leave authoritative state and both epochs unchanged. Client item movement, persistence routing, slot compatibility, swaps, map-ground transfer, capacity, recursive nesting, nested close propagation, up-arrow/item-delta controls, stack splitting, item actions, and real-client confirmation remain deferred
profiles.nativeCloseContainerViewDetail: native 740 CloseContainer decodes one client-view container ID, returns the parser-verified 0x6F close record, and filters that ID from later top-level container refreshes for the current session only. It does not mutate shared or persisted container state; nesting, up-arrow, and item-delta controls remain deferred
profiles.nativeUpdateContainerViewDetail: native 740 UpdateContainer decodes one client-view container ID and reopens only that current complete catalog-mapped top-level container through the parser-verified 0x6E record. A successful reopen removes the ID from the current session’s closed-view set; unavailable, nested, incomplete, or unmapped containers produce no packet and no state mutation. Shared/persisted container state, nesting, up-arrow, and item-delta controls remain deferred
profiles.playerStateDetail: persisted health, mana, capacity, and magic level feed a parser-shaped classic 740 HUD record with a 16-bit level and bounded soul byte. A shared-world vocation level-up advances the stats epoch, then the existing native refresh rehydrates authoritative level, experience, and vitals before encoding the frame. There is no native gameplay experience source yet, and unmodified-client confirmation remains required
profiles.playerPositionDetail: authoritative native movement persists SQLite position and orderly plus abrupt-disconnect native-session relog regressions restore the saved tile. Unmodified-client confirmation remains required
profiles.fightModeStateDetail: parser-backed native 740 fight-mode, chase-mode, and secure-mode state uses verified attack/chase-off/secure-off defaults and accepted input updates synchronize through authoritative shared state. One parser-verified three-byte 0xA7 player-modes record is appended to native 740 initialization and is sent again only after a real accepted state change; identical repeated input does not create a redundant record. Later PvP-mode variants, mitigation, attack behavior, pursuit, persistence, and real-client confirmation remain deferred
profiles.playerOutfitDetail: schema-v11 persists accepted classic-740 look type and color values, then hydrates them after map initialization with a configured look-type fallback for legacy or out-of-range records. A native 0xD2 request receives a classic 0xC8 current-outfit plus one-byte inclusive start/end look-type range. Operators may set otclientV8OutfitFirstLookType and otclientV8OutfitLastLookType; both must fit the classic byte form and contain the configured current look type, while zero values preserve the current-look default for existing worlds. A concrete ChangeOutfit request inside that range persists and echoes the selected appearance; an out-of-range request retains the current stored appearance. No newer outfit-list, addon, or mount fields are emitted. Asset validation, addons, mounts, and unmodified-client confirmation remain deferred
profiles.vocationCombatFormulaMetadataDetail: bounded nested TFS-style formula defense and armor values are parsed as validated fixed-point metadata, with independent 1.000 defaults when absent. They do not affect current FE mitigation, equipment, client packets, or profile compatibility claims; fight modes, active blocking, equipment aggregation, controlled randomness, and profile-specific formulas remain deferred
profiles.vocationTimingMetadataDetail: bounded TFS-style vocation attackspeed and basespeed attributes are retained as typed metadata, with verified defaults of 1500 milliseconds and 220 when absent. They do not alter current FE movement, combat cooldowns, packets, or profile compatibility claims; profile-specific timing, item-versus-vocation precedence, and movement formula behavior remain deferred
profiles.lifecycleDetail: server-side death, temple respawn, and schema-v9 persisted dead/respawn/loss state with strict native hydration. A configured explicit deathLosePercent value from 1 through 100 now applies the bounded exact fixed-percent loss model after supported native player-melee, condition, or static-creature heartbeat deaths, then commits level, experience, vitals, visible skills, exact progression attempts, and marked lifecycle state in one SQLite transaction. Zero preserves no-loss behavior. The native 740 path still emits only the evidence-backed zero-payload 0x28 death notification and sends no client loss record. Automatic timers, respawn/teleport packets, default-loss formula (-1), blessing/promotion adjustments, and unmodified-client confirmation remain deferred
profiles.progressionDetail: typed seven-skill levels/percentages and numeric vocation identity are authoritative, SQLite-persisted, locally provisionable, and delivered to the selected native 740 path. Operator-owned TFS-style vocations.xml supplies online health/mana regeneration intervals, skill multipliers, and parsed gainhp, gainmana, and gaincap metadata. A bounded direct config.lua experienceStages literal table accepts documented minlevel, optional maxlevel, and multiplier fields without Lua execution, rejects expressions, duplicate/unknown fields, overlap, invalid values, and excess data, and replaces rateExp when present; experienceStages = nil selects flat rateExp. The existing data/XML/stages.xml adapter is a fallback only when the legacy assignment is absent and retains its established rateExp composition. All selected sources drive deterministic authoritative operator experience awards with SQLite persistence, and existing experience awards and loss resolve levels through a checked integer classic cumulative threshold. When the stable CLI finds a matching parsed vocation and a positive level increase, FE atomically persists scaled gains to current/max health, current/max mana, and capacity; absent metadata or no level increase leaves vitals unchanged. The matching shared-world host transition advances the profile-gated stats-refresh epoch and rehydrates the next 740 frame from authoritative level, experience, and vitals, but no native gameplay experience source or real-client confirmation exists yet. Each successful fixed selected-player melee hit can award one configured fist try with exact persisted counters. Hydrated bounded poison/burning/energy damage schedules advance on the native heartbeat with persisted vitals, schema-v10 restores each validated elapsed interval remainder across restart, and lethal bounded condition damage activates the existing persisted server-side death state only at a validated assigned town temple. For configured explicit fixed loss only, the same progression rules now back an atomic post-death loss snapshot; default loss, promotion, and blessing behavior remain unimplemented. Weapon/spell formulas, combat/quest/monster reward sources, condition effect packets, client death screens/timers/respawn packets, soul, and full TFS-compatible advancement transactions remain deferred
profiles.combatDetail: typed physical adjacent-melee events use bounded damage, deterministic per-player server-tick cooldowns, profile-neutral flat physical mitigation, and an optional scriptless FE declarative weapon catalog. On the current native selected-melee path, only a server-owned matching right-hand item may select a catalog weapon; otherwise no catalog event is created. Separately, an active adjacent selected static target receives fixed 10-percentage-point damage no more than once per authoritative world tick through the same per-player combat cooldown. A supported native lethal player-combat transition may now apply and atomically persist the explicit configured fixed death-loss model after validated town/temple state; it sends no additional client loss packet. When the opt-in native static-target policy applies real damage, it persists the resulting vitals for the deterministic affected-player set and persists the existing death state for a lethal valid-temple transition; weapon catalog, mitigation, weapon timing, rewards, client effects, loot, corpses, formulas, scripts, and full AI remain separate. A typed spell-cast foundation atomically enforces nonzero bounded mana costs and server-tick cooldowns; an optional declarative spell catalog may construct those events from ID, mana cost, and interval, is retained as immutable native-host configuration, and can be resolved through a synchronized server-only host helper. No spell layer is profile-gated, persistent, or client-routable. TFS Lua weapon scripts, legacy XML formula semantics, map use, client weapon-use packets, armor, shielding, spell names/words/targets/formulas/effects/packets, ranged delivery, resistance, PvP, automatic attacks, and client combat effects remain deferred
profiles.mapItemUseDetail: typed server-side validation accepts only same-tile or adjacent use of an exact top-level authoritative map item stack and returns immutable metadata without mutation; the same validation is available through synchronized host state. Native 740 0x82 input is decoded as position, client thing ID, stack position, and index, then reaches that validator only when the configured presentation catalog maps the client thing ID to exactly one server item ID. Missing or ambiguous mappings, absent maps, and invalid server-owned targets are rejected without an outbound packet or mutation. Action execution, doors, switches, containers, charges, Lua, persistence, messages/effects, and full client item-use behavior remain deferred
profiles.equipmentBootstrapDetail: catalog-mapped persisted equipment is emitted at native 740 login in deterministic multi-slot order. Extended diagnostics report the count of omitted unmapped items without packet bodies; live inventory updates and container windows remain deferred
profiles.containerBootstrapDetail: top-level persisted containers are emitted at native 740 login only when the container and every contained item have validated presentation mappings. Nested or incomplete-mapping windows are omitted; container actions, live updates, and real-client confirmation remain deferred
profiles.questLogDetail: the native 740 request is decoded and receives a parser-shaped empty quest count response; quest storage, mission lines, scripting, gameplay semantics, and unmodified-client confirmation remain deferred
profiles.nativeSelectedStaticMeleeDetail: an active adjacent static creature selected by the native player receives bounded fixed 10-percentage-point damage no more than once per authoritative world tick. Each real hit writes the parser-shaped native 740 CreatureHealth record immediately and persists the authoritative static runtime snapshot; a defeated creature is removed through the existing visibility refresh. Loot, corpses, formulas, rewards, scripts, autonomous AI, broader-profile coverage, and real-client confirmation remain deferred
profiles.legacyMonsterExperienceMetadataDetail: the bounded non-executing TFS monster definition parser retains an unsigned root experience attribute for monster records. Malformed or overflowing values are rejected, while missing values and all NPC records retain zero. This is metadata only: no player reward, loot, corpse, formula, script, AI, or client behavior is activated
profiles.creaturesDetail: catalog-derived static spawn representation, native visibility, bounded authoritative 0–100% display health delivered on login and visibility refresh, optional deterministic movement, caller-triggered reactivation, propagated legacy per-spawn intervals for deterministic due-reactivation at an unoccupied spawn position, and native target selection of active authoritative static IDs. A core-only opt-in selector records the nearest living registered player on the same floor within a capped range, resolves equal distances by player ID, and clears its target on player removal or creature deactivation. The ordinary shared heartbeat leaves this state unchanged; an explicit nearest-living-player policy can perform one deterministic capped-range acquisition pass and reports only target-state changes. A separate explicit pursuit policy performs that acquisition and attempts at most one distance-reducing cardinal step per active static creature, reusing map/occupancy checks and advancing the visibility epoch once only if any real move occurs. Through the shared native world, a real step emits the established full-map refresh for a selected viewer; no-target, adjacent, and blocked outcomes emit nothing. A bounded static attack is available through the shared-world lock and may apply fixed damage only to an already selected, living, adjacent target; it advances the vitals-refresh epoch only after real damage. A potential lethal hit first validates the assigned temple, then enters the existing death state and clears the static target. staticCreatureTargetAttackDamage = 0 preserves disabled behavior. A configured value from 1 through 100 makes the native heartbeat select only an immediately adjacent living player and apply at most one fixed hit per active static creature per heartbeat. After a real attack pass, FE persists final vitals for each deterministically affected player. When the configured deathLosePercent is an explicit 1 through 100, a lethal attack also commits the bounded fixed-percent post-death level, experience, vitals, skills, exact attempts, and marked lifecycle snapshot; no default-formula, blessing, promotion, or client loss packet is emitted. A connected native session observes only its own living-to-dead shared-world transition and then emits the evidence-backed zero-payload 0x28 death record once; it sends no native combat effects, respawn, teleport, timer, or loss record. An external health value of zero remains display-only and does not deactivate the entity; however, a real adjacent selected static-melee hit that reaches zero deactivates the entity, clears its target intent, removes it from active visibility, and lets the existing reactivation policy later restore its configured spawn percentage. One native game-host heartbeat advances shared-world tick, evaluates due reactivation, and can perform this explicitly configured fixed attack; client sessions no longer advance shared time. The visibility epoch changes only after real damage, deactivation, health update, or reactivation. Default scheduling, multi-step routing, autonomous combat, obstacle pathfinding, creature formulas/mitigation, client effects, loot, corpses, scripts, rewards, persistent monster state, broader-profile coverage, end-to-end service lifecycle testing, and real-client observation remain deferred
profiles.scripting: partial — imported script references still enter the aggregate no-op audit dispatcher by default. A separate direct expression sandbox creates a fresh vendored Lua VM with no standard libraries, capped source/memory/instruction budgets, and typed primitive-only results. An explicit callback dispatcher can register one UTF-8 callback-function file only through a caller-selected canonical root; it rejects traversal, canonical escapes, non-files, duplicate names, and existing source-limit violations, then dispatches in a fresh sandbox. The additive script dispatch command may resolve only one exact, safe relative path already declared by a selected TFS XML registry with a script attribute, then pass it through that same loader with bounded primitive input. It does not auto-discover scripts, execute ordinary registry content, expose filesystem, network, process, package, debug, host, TFS API, module loading, event discovery, or gameplay mutation; full TFS Lua compatibility remains deferred

profiles.nativeOtClientV8Detail: explicit profile foundation recognizes that classic 8.0 requires RSA/XTEA transport, includes a bounded outbound-only opaque XTEA envelope primitive, and can extract only the marker plus four XTEA words from an already decrypted fixed block for future parser-backed work. Native enablement remains refused: there is no client-input decryption, credential/login/game parser, listener, packet-layout claim, or client interoperability claim
